title: Proactive kernel candidate filter and clock adapter for mixed-MIG fleets (H100 / L40S / A10)
creator: Ana Park
description: Improve tail latency and cost for mixed-MIG GPU pools by (1) pruning kernel candidates early using a lightweight feature filter, and (2) steering GPU clock governors via a conservative adapter that respects MIG tenancy and thermal budgets. Target SKUs: NVIDIA H100 (MIG slices), L40S, A10. This ticket pairs kernel-selection logic with clock/partition-aware scheduling so prefill and decode paths pick kernels that match both compute profile and current hardware envelope.
background: We frequently see variability in per-token latency across mixed fleets when the kernel selector tries many micro-kernel candidates during prefill or decode. On MIG-sliced H100 hosts the cost of probing kernels can be amplified by clock governor changes and slice sharing. Past work improved kernel ranking heuristics, but a gap remains: early-stage lightweight rejection of unlikely kernel candidates and a hardware-aware clock steering policy that reduces probe amplification without violating MIG isolation.
goals: 1) Implement a lightweight kernel candidate filter that rejects >=70% of low-probability candidates within 200us on warm paths. 2) Add a clock adapter that avoids aggressive clock shifts during prefills and prefers steady-state clocks for multi-tenant MIG slices. 3) Integrate signals into scheduler so kernel selection and clock decisions use the same hardware telemetry snapshot.
success_criteria: 1) Median prefill latency reduced by >=8% on mixed H100-MIG workloads. 2) 95th percentile per-token latency reduced by >=12% under realistic traffic traces. 3) Kernel probe count per request reduced by >=60%. 4) No increase in hardware thermal events or QoS violations on dedicated clusters.
milestones: M1: Design review for candidate filter + clock adapter (2025-02-21)
M2: Prototype candidate filter (in-memory feature table) + unit tests (2025-02-28)
M3: Integrate clock adapter hooks into scheduler + safety guardrails (2025-03-07)
M4: End-to-end perf run on staging mixed-fleet (H100-MIG + L40S + A10) (2025-03-14)
M5: Rollout to canary dedicated pool + monitor (2025-03-21)
M6: Full rollout and postmortem (runtime-1.22 patch window)
design_notes:
- Kernel candidate filter will compute a compact fingerprint (token-length histogram, kv-cache hit pattern, requested max_tokens, recent batch size) and use a small learned logistic model (weights table) to score candidates. The filter should be an in-process fast path called before expensive kernel preflight.
- Clock adapter: implement a mediator that requests 'prefer-stable' clock hint from node agent for selected queues during prefill-heavy phases. Hints are advisory; node agent enforces local thermal/MIG policies.
- Safety: adapter must back off if GPU temperature > threshold or if MIG tenancy indicates strict QoS.
- We will persist per-SKU microbenchmarks (H100 MIG slice profiles, L40S short-context vs long-context, A10 batch-heavy) to inform default weights.
- Do not change kernel opcode semantics; filter only gates which micro-kernel candidates are attempted.
implementation_steps: 1) Add a KernelFilter interface with evaluate(features) -> score threshold. 2) Implement lightweight feature extractor in serving runtime prefill path. 3) Wire default weights table shipped in runtime-1.22; allow config overrides via node-level feature-flags. 4) Implement ClockAdapter service used by scheduler: requestStableClock(queue_id, reason) and release. 5) Node agent API: accept hint with TTL and policy-id. 6) Add telemetry counters and histogram metrics for filtered_candidates, avg_filter_latency, clock_hint_success_rate. 7) Bench and iterate on threshold for each SKU using staging harness.
testing_plan:
- Unit tests for feature extractor and filter scoring thresholds.
- Microbench harness: synthetic short/long context traces across H100-MIG, L40S, A10 to measure candidate pruning ratios and probe latency.
- Integration: deploy to staging mixed-fleet and run replayed production traces for 24h.
- Canary: 2 dedicated queues with canary load (5% of traffic) for 72h. Monitor for latency regressions, thermal alerts, and request errors.
- Fallback: if any increase in error rate or thermal emergency counts, automatically disable filter or adapter via remote flag.
telemetry_and_dashboards:
- New metrics: runtime.kernel_filter.filtered_count, runtime.kernel_filter.avg_latency_us, runtime.kernel_filter.probe_reduction_ratio, runtime.clock_adapter.hint_requests, runtime.clock_adapter.hint_applied, runtime.hardware.qos_violation_count.
- Dashboard: Per-SKU panels for H100-MIG(slice-size), L40S, A10 showing prefill median/95th, kernel-probe-per-request, and clock hint success.
- Alerts: alert if filtered_count drops below expected or if hint_applied_rate < 50% during canary.
rollout_and_rollback:
Phase 1: Enable filter default but set conservative thresholds and disable clock adapter. Phase 2: Enable adapter on canary queues only. Phase 3: Widen to dedicated pools, monitor for 72h.
Rollback: Remote feature flag toggles to disable filter or adapter. If thermal or QoS alerts trigger, automatically rollback adapter and keep filter conservative. Document rollback playbook in runbook linked in comments.
risks:
- Over-aggressive filtering could omit best kernel causing higher latency under certain long-context workloads.
- Clock hints could be ignored by node agent, leading to no improvement but added complexity.
- MIG isolation policies might prevent desired steady clocks; need tight coordination with infra.
- Model weights may overfit to staging traces; require continuous calibration.
open_questions:
1) Where to store per-SKU weight tables for quick updates? (options: baked in runtime binary, node agent config, remote config store)
2) How to surface per-candidate rejection reasons for debugging without adding too much telemetry cost?
3) Should we expose control to customers on Dedicated (opt-in stable-clock) given potential cost/thermal trade-offs?

2025-02-20 Performance Eng: Microbench results attached to design doc; L40S benefits smaller due to shorter prefill windows. Suggested moving some feature calculations to earlier pipeline stage.
